title: Shrinking neighbourhoods: μ(W) ≤ C·μ(W∖K) for all W ⊂⊂ U forces μ(K) = 0 (Simon 6, proof of 2.36 after (4))
statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let K ⊆ U be compact, let μ be a measure on ℝ^P with μ(W) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U, and let C ∈ [0, ∞) be such that μ(W) ≤ C·μ(W∖K) for every open W ⊂⊂ U. Then μ(K) = 0.
lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U K : Set (Eucl P)) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (C : ℝ≥0), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → (∀ W, CompactlyContainedOpen W U → μ W < ∞) → (∀ W, CompactlyContainedOpen W U → μ W ≤ (C : ℝ≥0∞) * μ (W \ K)) → μ K = 0
